evidence.description: The event enumeration contains only an empty-string case.
The empty raw value is forwarded without validation.

candidates.explanation: The only CustomEvent case has an empty raw value, and logCustomEvent forwards it directly to Braze. Consequently, every event expressible through this API has an empty name rather than a usable custom-event identifier.
candidates.title: Custom-event API only exposes an empty event name

evidence.description: The consent flow invokes the notification-center setup helper.
The shared notification center's categories are replaced with only Braze categories.

candidates.explanation: setNotificationCategories replaces the notification center's entire category set; it does not add categories. Calling this helper therefore discards any previously registered categories outside the Braze set. This application-wide side effect occurs as part of requesting notification consent.
candidates.title: Notification setup replaces all application notification categories

evidence.description: The singleton stores mutable SDK and authorization state without actor isolation.
Initialization launches an unstructured task that refreshes authorization state.
The SDK reference is assigned in an unisolated method and then accessed by a separately scheduled MainActor task.
An asynchronous method writes the shared authorization-status property without isolation.

candidates.explanation: The singleton's mutable state is accessed from unisolated methods, an unstructured task, and a MainActor task without a common actor or synchronization mechanism. The MainActor annotation on the UI setup task does not protect accesses elsewhere. Concurrent initialization or notification-status refreshes can therefore race on braze and notificationAuthorizationStatus.
candidates.title: Shared mutable service state lacks concurrency isolation
